analysis.title: Credit MarketStrats: Important to differentiate between risk and uncertainty
key_insights: Price action over the past couple of weeks suggests investors are starting to price an economic/growth slowdown. Equity/bond correlation turned negative over the past month after being positive for most of 2026.
5y USD rates rallied about 40bps over the past month, with real rates contributing about 30bps of that. The rally coincided with a sell-off in NDX/US tech.
The author reads the market as pricing the AI story and US growth as two sides of the same coin, and says the verdict on how the AI story plays out is still open.
Credit fund flows are improving. The rates rally lifted credit total returns, and there were net inflows over the past month in EUR IG, USD IG, EUR HY and USD HY.

Last week saw EUR40bn of issuance across EUR IG unsecured financials and corporates, the second busiest week on record for EUR IG. New issues performed strongly on the break and concessions fell from mid double digits to high single digits. Most segments ended the week tighter.

Rates/credit spread correlation has turned negative, so rates/duration is again a natural hedge for credit portfolios. The author expects stronger demand from IG all-in yield investors and remains broadly constructive on IG credit.

The author distinguishes risk from uncertainty: the backdrop is moving into a period of very high uncertainty rather than high risk. Hard and soft data do not show meaningful deterioration (last week's NFP was strong, unemployment did not rise, UMich sentiment improved).
Sources of uncertainty named are the AI/hyperscaler outlook and geopolitics. The author argues the US mid-term results may have increased uncertainty rather than reduced it.
Suggested portfolio framework: own uncertainty convexity (for example cross-asset gamma) and fund it with carry from being long risk IG credit, especially in all-in yield format.
Credit longs favored: iTraxx Main 10y index, iTraxx Main 5y5y forward, buying iTraxx receivers funded by selling payer spreads, EUR IG senior financials cash, and EUR IG corporate hybrids.

The market may stay wary on growth for the next couple of weeks. Real rates still screen wide even after the rally, and the growth-vs-rates picture is not constructive. The author advocates asymmetric hedges, such as short risk in HY credit funded by longs elsewhere in credit.

New relative value trade: short risk CDX HY vs long risk iTraxx SnrFin index. SnrFin underperformed over the past 3 months, partly because of OAT/France weakness, and the author sees this as a valuation dislocation to fade. The CDX HY to SnrFin spread ratio is a reasonable entry point, and non-dealers are net short SnrFin and net long CDX HY.

France: French credit performed strongly last week alongside OAT-Bund compression, but the author stays skeptical and sees it as a fade-the-rally space. French Fins have underperformed the rest of IG, French non-Fins have not, and shorting baskets of French non-Fins is a convex downside expression.

Hyperscalers: META issued its first EUR bond (EUR6bn) and Alphabet issued EUR9bn. Together they were over 60% of last week's EUR IG corporate issuance. The author's research team expects more diversification away from USD markets, and the GS EUR hyperscaler basket (GSLCEUHS) is offered as an expression.

tension_points.bull_case: Improving fund flows, strong EUR IG issuance absorption, rates acting as a natural hedge and compelling all-in yields support long IG credit, with carry funding uncertainty convexity.
tension_points.bear_case: Real rates still screen wide and the growth-vs-rates picture is not constructive. An AI-driven growth scare could continue to be priced for the next couple of weeks, which supports short HY risk positions.
